Q: Why is my CSS styling not working when I use mobile screen? Clicking the hamburger does show the nav element A:

The issue is called CSS Specificity. Browsers use a scoring system to decide which style wins when rules conflict:

  • ID Selector (#sidebar): High Score (100 points)

  • Class Selector (.show): Medium Score (10 points)

  • Element Selector (nav): Low Score (1 point)

Why it failed with #sidebar

When you used #sidebar { display: none; }, its high score (100) overpowered the .show { display: block; } (10). The browser ignored the class because the ID was "stronger."

Why it worked with nav

When you changed it to nav { display: none; }, its score dropped to 1. Since the class .show (10) is now stronger than the element nav (1), the sidebar finally appeared.

The Best Fix

Keep your IDs, but make the "show" rule more specific so it has the highest score:

#sidebar.show {
  display: block;
}

Q: How to skip a cell in MS Excel IF function when the condition is false A:

@Pratyya10 if you add an empty string ( "" ) to your formula after the last comma it should leave that cell "untouched".

=IF(NOT(MOD(ROW(),4) = 0), 1,"")

Hope this helps!

Q: using call_form in menu forms 6i A:

You should set the window property Modal to Yes instead of No.

Q: How to find all fonts paths on Windows A:

To be able to get the font in the registry key, just right click the font file and select "install for all users" - you must be admin to do that.

Otherwise use the "HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Fonts" to retrieve the fonts available only to the current user (add them to the ones found in the HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE) ;)
